message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how you can create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that is equipped with an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU (if it were available) and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
Because Google Cloud does not currently offer the RTX A6000 as a GPU type, the example uses the closest supported GPU – the **NVIDIA Tesla A100** – and explains how you would swap it out if the RTX A6000 were offered.

---

## 1.  Prerequisites

| Item | How to set it up |
|------|------------------|
| **Google Cloud project** | Create a project in the Cloud Console or use an existing one. |
| **Billing enabled** | Make sure billing is attached to the project. |
| **Compute Engine API enabled** | In the Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Library → enable *Compute Engine API*. |
| **Service account key** | Create a service account with the *Compute Admin* role (`roles/compute.admin`) and download a JSON key. |
| **gcloud SDK** | Install the Cloud SDK on your local machine or use Cloud Shell. |

---

## 2.  Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Authenticate with the service account
export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/path/to/your-service-account-key.json"

# 2️⃣  Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 3️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "rtx-a6000-ubuntu20" \
  --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
  --zone="${ZONE}" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size=200GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: custom startup script
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a100,count=1" \   # <-- replace with RTX A6000 if available
  --reservation-affinity=any
```

> **Note**  
> - Replace `nvidia-tesla-a100` with `nvidia-rtx-a6000` if Google Cloud ever adds that GPU type.  
> - The `--reservation-affinity=any` flag tells Compute Engine to use any available GPU reservation; remove it if you want to use a specific reservation.

---

## 3.  Using the REST API (curl)

If you prefer to hit the REST endpoint directly, here’s a `curl` example that performs the same operation:

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set variables
PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu20"
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# 2️⃣  Build the JSON payload
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "${INSTANCE_NAME}",
  "machineType": "zones/${ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 200,
        "diskType": "zones/${ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      },
      "autoDelete": true
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100"
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y build-essential"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# 3️⃣  Send the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "${INSTANCE_JSON}"
```

### What the JSON does

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name |
| `machineType` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS, 200 GB SSD) |
| `networkInterfaces[0]` | Default VPC network + external IP |
| `serviceAccounts[0]` | Permissions for the instance |
| `guestAccelerators[0]` | GPU attachment (replace type if RTX A6000 becomes available) |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Optional startup script |

---

## 4.  Quick sanity check

After the instance is created, you can verify its status:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe "${INSTANCE_NAME}" \
  --project="${PROJECT_ID}" \
  --zone="${ZONE}" \
  --format="json"
```

Look for the `"guestAccelerators"` section to confirm the GPU is attached.

---

## 5.  Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---------|--------------|-----|
| `ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) Resource not found: projects/.../acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a100` | Wrong accelerator type | Double‑check the accelerator type name in the Compute Engine docs. |
| `ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) quotaExceeded` | GPU quota exceeded | Request a higher quota in the Cloud Console → IAM & Admin → Quotas. |
| `ERROR: (gcloud.compute.instances.create) Permission denied` | Service account missing role | Add `roles/compute.admin` to the service account. |

---

### Bottom line

- **Use the `gcloud` CLI** for quick, interactive creation.  
- **Use the REST API** if you need to embed the call in a script or CI/CD pipeline.  
- **Replace the accelerator type** with `nvidia-rtx-a6000` once Google Cloud offers it.  

Happy computing!
